topic.angle: 17 is the fewest, proved by computer

card.title: How few clues can a Sudoku have?

body.claim: A standard Sudoku with only 16 clues can never have a single unique solution. 17 is the minimum.
body.why: Many puzzles with 17 clues and one solution have been found. A 2014 paper proved, through an exhaustive computer search, that 16 clues can never be enough. There are an enormous number of ways to fill a Sudoku grid.

probes.question: What is the smallest number of clues a standard Sudoku can have and still have exactly one solution?

claims.claim: A proper Sudoku needs at least 17 clues; 16 can never give a unique solution; probe answer 17
claims.quote: proved that the minimum number of clues in any proper sudoku is 17

claims.claim: A 2014 paper proved this through an exhaustive computer search
claims.quote: A 2014 paper by Gary McGuire, Bastian Tugemann, and Gilles Civario proved that the minimum number of clues in any proper sudoku is 17 through an exhaustive computer search

claims.claim: Many puzzles with 17 clues and one solution have been found
claims.quote: Many sudokus have been found with 17 clues, although finding them is not a trivial task.

claims.claim: There are an enormous number of ways to fill a Sudoku grid
claims.quote: the number of filled grids is 6,670,903,752,021,072,936,960
